title: Query Rewriting: HyDE, Multi-Query, and Decomposition

questions.question: What is the core mechanism of HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings)?
options: Embed the user query through a larger model
Run the query through multiple retrievers and pick the best one
Generate a fake answer with an LLM, embed that hypothetical document, and retrieve against its vector instead of the query vector
Hash the query and look it up in a cache
questions.explanation: HyDE writes a document-shaped passage in the corpus voice and retrieves on that embedding; the query vector is replaced.

questions.question: Why is it acceptable for the LLM-generated hypothetical document in HyDE to be factually wrong?
options: The reranker repairs factual errors
The user never sees the hypothetical
The LLM call is rolled back when wrong
The retriever cares about the token distribution, not factual correctness; the hypothetical's vector lands near the real passage
questions.explanation: Retrieval is similarity in embedding space; if the hypothetical's vocabulary matches the corpus, the vector lands in the right region.

questions.question: What is the difference between multi-query expansion and query decomposition?
options: Multi-query produces N paraphrases of the same question; decomposition produces sub-questions that together cover a multi-topic question
Multi-query uses cosine; decomposition uses BM25
Decomposition runs locally; multi-query requires a remote model
They are identical
questions.explanation: Paraphrases preserve intent; sub-questions split a multi-topic query into independently answerable pieces.

questions.question: When does query decomposition over-split and hurt retrieval?
options: When the query is too long for the LLM
When the query is atomic (single-topic), the decomposer invents fake sub-questions and the retrievals all return the same document with reduced rank
When the corpus is too small
When BM25 is disabled
questions.explanation: Decomposing an atomic query splits it into fake sub-questions; their retrievals dilute the merge so the right document ranks lower.

questions.question: Why do the three rewriting strategies fuse with RRF rather than score interpolation?
options: RRF is the only operation supported by Python
RRF runs on GPUs and score interpolation does not
Score interpolation requires per-corpus calibration; RRF combines rank-based contributions without calibration, which is required when fusing N retrievals from different rewrites
Score interpolation cannot handle more than two lists
questions.explanation: Same argument as lesson 65; rank-based fusion does not need per-corpus alpha tuning and stays stable across rewriter outputs.

questions.question: For a query in MQ_TABLE and MultiQueryRewriter(n=3), how many rewrites are returned?
options: Three: the original query is replaced by three paraphrases
Seven: the original, three paraphrases, and three hypothetical documents
One: only the original query is retained
Four: the original query plus three table paraphrases
questions.explanation: MultiQueryRewriter.rewrite builds [query] + self.llm.paraphrase(query, n=3). For an MQ_TABLE key, that is the original plus three paraphrases, four rewrite strings total.
